name: decode_status
why: STATUS_CD is decoded through CODES CUST_STATUS, so the source integer and the target string never compare raw.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN m.status_cd IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(m.status_cd) || ')') END AS "status", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master m LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'CUST_STATUS' AND c.code_val = m.status_cd GROUP BY CASE WHEN m.status_cd IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(m.status_cd) || ')') END

name: decode_sub_status
why: SUB_STATUS_CD is decoded through CODES CUST_STATUS.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN m.sub_status_cd IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(m.sub_status_cd) || ')') END AS "subStatus", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master m LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'CUST_STATUS' AND c.code_val = m.sub_status_cd GROUP BY CASE WHEN m.sub_status_cd IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(m.sub_status_cd) || ')') END

name: decode_type
why: CUST_TYPE_CD is decoded through CODES CUST_TYPE.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN m.cust_type_cd IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(m.cust_type_cd) || ')') END AS "type", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master m LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'CUST_TYPE' AND c.code_val = m.cust_type_cd GROUP BY CASE WHEN m.cust_type_cd IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(m.cust_type_cd) || ')') END

name: yn_taxExempt
why: tax_exempt_yn becomes flags.taxExempt; the harness has no yn_to_bool rule.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN tax_exempt_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' WHEN TRIM(tax_exempt_yn) = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN TRIM(tax_exempt_yn) = 'N' THEN 'false' ELSE 'other' END AS "value", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master GROUP BY CASE WHEN tax_exempt_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' WHEN TRIM(tax_exempt_yn) = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN TRIM(tax_exempt_yn) = 'N' THEN 'false' ELSE 'other' END

name: yn_creditHold
why: credit_hold_yn becomes flags.creditHold; the harness has no yn_to_bool rule.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN credit_hold_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' WHEN TRIM(credit_hold_yn) = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN TRIM(credit_hold_yn) = 'N' THEN 'false' ELSE 'other' END AS "value", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master GROUP BY CASE WHEN credit_hold_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' WHEN TRIM(credit_hold_yn) = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN TRIM(credit_hold_yn) = 'N' THEN 'false' ELSE 'other' END

name: yn_dunningExempt
why: dunning_exempt_yn becomes flags.dunningExempt; the harness has no yn_to_bool rule.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN dunning_exempt_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' WHEN TRIM(dunning_exempt_yn) = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN TRIM(dunning_exempt_yn) = 'N' THEN 'false' ELSE 'other' END AS "value", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master GROUP BY CASE WHEN dunning_exempt_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' WHEN TRIM(dunning_exempt_yn) = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN TRIM(dunning_exempt_yn) = 'N' THEN 'false' ELSE 'other' END

name: yn_vip
why: vip_yn becomes flags.vip; the harness has no yn_to_bool rule.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN vip_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' WHEN TRIM(vip_yn) = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN TRIM(vip_yn) = 'N' THEN 'false' ELSE 'other' END AS "value", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master GROUP BY CASE WHEN vip_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' WHEN TRIM(vip_yn) = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN TRIM(vip_yn) = 'N' THEN 'false' ELSE 'other' END

name: parse_signup_dt
why: SIGNUP_DT is a 'DD-MON-YY' string; graded as a month distribution over all 25,000 rows, with the unparseable rows in the '~null' bucket.
source_sql: SELECT NVL(TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(signup_dt DEFAULT NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM'), '~null') AS "month", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master GROUP BY NVL(TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(signup_dt DEFAULT NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM'), '~null')

name: parse_last_activity_dt
why: LAST_ACTIVITY_DT is a 'DD-MON-YY' string.
source_sql: SELECT NVL(TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(last_activity_dt DEFAULT NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM'), '~null') AS "month", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master GROUP BY NVL(TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(last_activity_dt DEFAULT NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM'), '~null')

name: signup_dt_unparseable_raw
why: the 50 unparseable SIGNUP_DT values: the date is null and the raw string is kept under legacy.signupDtRaw.
source_sql: SELECT signup_dt AS "raw", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master WHERE signup_dt IS NOT NULL AND TO_DATE(signup_dt DEFAULT NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR, 'DD-MON-YY') IS NULL GROUP BY signup_dt

name: parse_remaining_date_strings
why: the three date strings that are null on every row: a parse that invented or dropped a value would show here.
source_sql: SELECT 'lastInvoiceAt' AS "field", COUNT(last_invoice_dt) AS "n" FROM customer_master UNION ALL SELECT 'lastPaymentAt', COUNT(last_payment_dt) FROM customer_master UNION ALL SELECT 'terminatedAt', COUNT(terminate_dt) FROM customer_master

name: csv_related_account_list_lengths
why: RELATED_ACCT_IDS splits into an array; -1 is the malformed bucket (empty item, stray separator, or an item that is not an account id), which becomes [] plus legacy.relatedAcctIdsRaw.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN related_acct_ids IS NULL THEN 0 WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(related_acct_ids, '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*(,[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*)*$') THEN REGEXP_COUNT(related_acct_ids, ',') + 1 ELSE -1 END AS "len", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master GROUP BY CASE WHEN related_acct_ids IS NULL THEN 0 WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(related_acct_ids, '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*(,[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*)*$') THEN REGEXP_COUNT(related_acct_ids, ',') + 1 ELSE -1 END

name: csv_related_account_malformed_raw
why: the 31 malformed RELATED_ACCT_IDS values, compared as a set.
source_sql: SELECT related_acct_ids AS "raw", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master WHERE related_acct_ids IS NOT NULL AND NOT REGEXP_LIKE(related_acct_ids, '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*(,[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*)*$') GROUP BY related_acct_ids

name: csv_related_account_items
why: the account ids themselves, in every position of the list: count and sum on each side.
source_sql: WITH v AS (SELECT CASE WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(related_acct_ids, '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*(,[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*)*$') THEN related_acct_ids END AS s FROM customer_master) SELECT p.pos AS "pos", COUNT(TO_NUMBER(TRIM(REGEXP_SUBSTR(v.s, '[^,]+', 1, p.pos)))) AS "n", SUM(TO_NUMBER(TRIM(REGEXP_SUBSTR(v.s, '[^,]+', 1, p.pos)))) AS "total" FROM v, LATERAL (SELECT LEVEL AS pos FROM dual CONNECT BY LEVEL <= REGEXP_COUNT(v.s, ',') + 1) p WHERE v.s IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.pos

name: csv_promo_codes_items
why: PROMO_CODES_CSV splits into promoCodes[]; every code is compared in its position.
source_sql: WITH v AS (SELECT CASE WHEN TRIM(promo_codes_csv) IS NOT NULL AND NOT REGEXP_LIKE(promo_codes_csv, '^[[:space:]]*,') AND NOT REGEXP_LIKE(promo_codes_csv, ',[[:space:]]*$') AND NOT REGEXP_LIKE(promo_codes_csv, ',[[:space:]]*,') THEN promo_codes_csv END AS s FROM customer_master) SELECT p.pos AS "pos", TRIM(REGEXP_SUBSTR(v.s, '[^,]+', 1, p.pos)) AS "item", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM v, LATERAL (SELECT LEVEL AS pos FROM dual CONNECT BY LEVEL <= REGEXP_COUNT(v.s, ',') + 1) p WHERE v.s IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.pos, TRIM(REGEXP_SUBSTR(v.s, '[^,]+', 1, p.pos))

name: csv_child_account_ids_absent
why: CHILD_ACCT_IDS is null on every row: childAccountIds must be empty everywhere, with no raw kept.
source_sql: SELECT COUNT(child_acct_ids) AS "populated", COUNT(*) AS "docs" FROM customer_master

name: address_physical_scalars
why: addresses[0] is the physical address; its scalar fields sit behind an array index, which the harness's field paths cannot address.
source_sql: SELECT city AS "city", state_cd AS "state", zip AS "zip", zip4 AS "zip4", country_cd AS "country", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master GROUP BY city, state_cd, zip, zip4, country_cd

name: address_physical_lines
why: addresses[0].lines keeps the non-null ADDR_LINE_n columns in column order; compared as line count plus the second line's value.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN addr_line_1 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_2 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_3 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_4 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_5 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_6 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS "lineCount", CASE WHEN addr_line_1 IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(addr_line_2, addr_line_3, addr_line_4, addr_line_5, addr_line_6) WHEN addr_line_2 IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(addr_line_3, addr_line_4, addr_line_5, addr_line_6) WHEN addr_line_3 IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(addr_line_4, addr_line_5, addr_line_6) WHEN addr_line_4 IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(addr_line_5, addr_line_6) WHEN addr_line_5 IS NOT NULL THEN addr_line_6 END AS "line2", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master GROUP BY CASE WHEN addr_line_1 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_2 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_3 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_4 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_5 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END + CASE WHEN addr_line_6 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, CASE WHEN addr_line_1 IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(addr_line_2, addr_line_3, addr_line_4, addr_line_5, addr_line_6) WHEN addr_line_2 IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(addr_line_3, addr_line_4, addr_line_5, addr_line_6) WHEN addr_line_3 IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(addr_line_4, addr_line_5, addr_line_6) WHEN addr_line_4 IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(addr_line_5, addr_line_6) WHEN addr_line_5 IS NOT NULL THEN addr_line_6 END

name: address_physical_line1_digest
why: ADDR_LINE_1 has 25,000 near-unique values, so it is compared as a digest rather than row by row.
source_sql: SELECT COUNT(addr_line_1) AS "n", COUNT(DISTINCT addr_line_1) AS "distinctLines", MIN(addr_line_1) AS "mn", MAX(addr_line_1) AS "mx" FROM customer_master

name: address_mailing_element
why: addresses[1] is the mailing address: the element is always present in the declared position, and every mailing column is null in the source.
source_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "elements", COUNT(mail_city) AS "city", COUNT(mail_state_cd) AS "state", COUNT(mail_zip) AS "zip", COUNT(mail_addr_line_1) AS "line1" FROM customer_master

name: phones_kind_decode
why: PHONE1..4 collapse into phones[]; each kind is decoded through CODES PHONE_TYPE, so the integer and the string never compare raw.
source_sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN phone1 IS NOT NULL AND phone1_type_cd = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone2 IS NOT NULL AND phone2_type_cd = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone3 IS NOT NULL AND phone3_type_cd = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone4 IS NOT NULL AND phone4_type_cd = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "main", SUM(CASE WHEN phone1 IS NOT NULL AND phone1_type_cd = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone2 IS NOT NULL AND phone2_type_cd = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone3 IS NOT NULL AND phone3_type_cd = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone4 IS NOT NULL AND phone4_type_cd = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "billing", SUM(CASE WHEN phone1 IS NOT NULL AND phone1_type_cd = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone2 IS NOT NULL AND phone2_type_cd = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone3 IS NOT NULL AND phone3_type_cd = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone4 IS NOT NULL AND phone4_type_cd = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "fax", SUM(CASE WHEN phone1 IS NOT NULL AND phone1_type_cd = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone2 IS NOT NULL AND phone2_type_cd = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone3 IS NOT NULL AND phone3_type_cd = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone4 IS NOT NULL AND phone4_type_cd = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "after-hours", SUM(CASE WHEN phone1 IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone2 IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone3 IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN phone4 IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "elements" FROM customer_master

name: phones_number_digest
why: the phone numbers themselves, as a digest over every non-null slot.
source_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "elements", COUNT(DISTINCT p) AS "distinctNumbers", MIN(p) AS "mn", MAX(p) AS "mx" FROM (SELECT phone1 AS p FROM customer_master WHERE phone1 IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT phone2 AS p FROM customer_master WHERE phone2 IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT phone3 AS p FROM customer_master WHERE phone3 IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT phone4 AS p FROM customer_master WHERE phone4 IS NOT NULL)

name: emails_digest
why: EMAIL_1..3 collapse into emails[]; compared as a digest over every non-null slot.
source_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "elements", COUNT(DISTINCT e) AS "distinctEmails", MIN(e) AS "mn", MAX(e) AS "mx" FROM (SELECT email_1 AS e FROM customer_master WHERE email_1 IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT email_2 AS e FROM customer_master WHERE email_2 IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT email_3 AS e FROM customer_master WHERE email_3 IS NOT NULL)

name: attributes_created_dt_parse
why: ENTITY_ATTR_VALUE.CREATED_DT is a 'DD-MON-YY' string inside the embedded attributes[]; graded as a month distribution over all 8,333 elements.
source_sql: SELECT NVL(TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(created_dt DEFAULT NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM'), '~null') AS "month", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM entity_attr_value WHERE entity_type = 'CUSTOMER' GROUP BY NVL(TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(created_dt DEFAULT NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM'), '~null')

name: attributes_per_customer
why: attributes[] is an array, not a map: a repeated (entity, attr_name) pair must stay a separate element, so the per-customer element count is compared as a distribution.
source_sql: SELECT NVL(e.cnt, 0) AS "size", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM customer_master m LEFT JOIN (SELECT entity_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM entity_attr_value WHERE entity_type = 'CUSTOMER' GROUP BY entity_id) e ON e.entity_id = m.cust_id GROUP BY NVL(e.cnt, 0)

name: history_rows
why: CUSTOMER_MASTER_HIST is trigger-fed and empty; the op compares the row set itself, so a row appearing on either side is a finding.
source_sql: SELECT hist_id AS "id", hist_op AS "op" FROM customer_master_hist
